preamble: Retraction of a palatalized alveolar fricative [sʲ] to postalveolar [ʃ]. In Goidelic, the slender (palatalized) partner of broad /sˠ/, written /sʲ/ for Old Irish, is postalveolar [ʃ] in Modern Irish and Scottish Gaelic; the Scottish Gaelic slender s is described as so palatalized that it has become postalveolar. Islay and Colonsay Gaelic keep [s] in the same words.

examples.note: The slender fricative of the palatalized series is postalveolar [ʃ] in Modern Irish.
Slender s before a front vowel became [ʃ].
Islay and Colonsay keep /sɲɛxk/, while Lewis, Harris, Uist and Barra have [ʃ].
Slender s is so palatalized that it has become postalveolar.
